title: Odile and the Harbor
premise: Five years after a fire took her family's event barn and her faith in love, wedding planner Juniper Iversen lives quietly in the coastal town of Harbor's End, planning other people's perfect days while refusing her own happiness. Her solace has been a decade-long anonymous correspondence with 'Wren,' a pen pal who knows her better than anyone—until Wren, revealed to be cartographer Elias Marsh, buys the cottage next door and arrives in person. As Juniper is hired to orchestrate the town's centennial harbor festival, she must decide whether to forgive herself for the fire she believes she caused, and the book ends with her walking down the festival aisle not as a planner but as a bride, choosing belonging over invisibility.
about_author: Quentin Sterling is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent a decade staging other people's happily-ever-afters along the New England coast before turning to fiction. Their novels explore the quiet architecture of belonging, and they still write letters by hand.

chapters.title: The Last Unsent Letter
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She finalizes a flawless wedding for strangers, then returns to her empty cottage and writes to Wren, her anonymous pen pal of ten years, confessing she's tired of being careful. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as contentment, and the first crack in her armor.

chapters.title: The New Neighbor
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A moving truck arrives next door; the newcomer, Elias Marsh, is warm, curious, and unsettlingly familiar. He mentions he's 'waiting for the right moment' to tell her something. Emotional beat: unease and reluctant intrigue as her safe perimeter is breached.

chapters.title: Maps of a Decade
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He unpacks boxes of letters—hers—and debates revealing he is Wren, having moved to Harbor's End after learning her town from her postmarks. Emotional beat: guilt over the deception, hope that proximity can become honesty.

chapters.title: The Centennial Contract
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The town council hires her to run the centennial harbor festival, pairing her with Elias, who's been commissioned to draw a commemorative map. Forced collaboration begins. Emotional beat: resistance softening into grudging admiration.

chapters.title: What the Fire Left
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A festival planning visit to the old event barn ruins triggers memories: the blaze five years ago, her sister's injury, the blame she carries. Elias finds her there, and she almost tells him everything. Emotional beat: grief surfacing, intimacy deepening.

chapters.title: Almost, and Then Not
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A near-kiss during a storm-drenched festival setup is interrupted by Elias's phone call with his editor—and Juniper glimpses a manuscript titled 'Letters to Juniper.' She flees, convinced she's a research subject. Emotional beat: betrayal, the walls slamming back up.

chapters.title: The Confession in the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He confronts Juniper, admits he is Wren, and explains he fell for her through the letters long before he ever planned to move. She accuses him of ten years of voyeurism and tells him the truth of the fire—she left a lantern burning. Emotional beat: raw mutual exposure, the relationship shattered.

chapters.title: The Festival Falls Apart
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Days before the centennial, a supplier collapses and the festival teeters; Juniper, spiraling over Elias, nearly walks away. Her found-family—the florist, the baker, her recovered sister—refuse to let her quit, revealing they've always known about her guilt. Emotional beat: being truly seen, and held.

chapters.title: Forgiving the Woman in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Her sister gives her the one thing she never had: absolution, and proof the fire's cause was faulty wiring, not her lantern. Juniper reads Wren's final unsent letter, delivered by Elias, which asks for nothing. Emotional beat: catharsis, the choice to stop punishing herself.

chapters.title: The Aisle at the Harbor
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The centennial festival succeeds in imperfect, human splendor. Elias stands at the end of the lantern-lit pier where the town, unbidden, has arranged a wedding—hers. She walks it, vows to stay visible, and kisses him as the harbor lights come on. Emotional beat: belonging, chosen at last.
